title: China Spent 1,700 Years Faking Jade With Fire | China Travel Expert
description:
China spent 1,700 years turning fire and ash into fake jade — that's celadon, and the green is glaze, not stone.

Longquan celadon dates back roughly 1,700 years. The jade-like green comes from iron in the glaze fired in a low-oxygen "reduction" kiln at close to 1,300°C; let in more air and the same glaze drifts toward brown. Its traditional firing techniques joined UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2009.

🧭 Expert Tip: To watch it made, head to Longquan in Zhejiang — kiln workshops there still fire celadon in traditional dragon kilns and many welcome visitors.
